Subject: SIG packaging & upload requirements for ACME procurement

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the SIG draft — procurement is ready to ingest the package but they have some portal constraints I want to confirm before we upload:

- OneTrust requires either (A) each PDF uploaded as an individual file with a visible watermark on each page, or (B) a single password-protected ZIP containing all files plus a manifest CSV with checksums. Which option works best for you?
- For Whistic they prefer a single ZIP with a manifest and individual file MD5s listed; the portal sometimes rejects password-protected ZIPs depending on buyer settings.
- Can you provide per-file MD5 (or SHA256) values in the manifest, and a checksum file we can programmatically verify on our side?
- Also: can the PDFs be flattened (no comments/hidden layers) and a visible watermark placed that reads: "For ACME Procurement - Confidential"?

If you can call out the upload method and provide a checksum manifest, I’ll schedule the final upload window this week.

Appreciate it — Jared
Jared Collins

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG packaging & upload requirements for ACME procurement

Thanks Jared — good questions. Short answer: we can support either flow, but here are recommended steps and trade-offs so procurement can pick: 

1) Preferred (OneTrust-friendly): provide individual, flattened PDFs with the visible watermark on every page plus a manifest.csv listing each filename, file size, and MD5. Upload each PDF separately to OneTrust. Pros: preserves searchability, avoids password issues. Cons: manual uploads per-file in some portals.

2) Alternate (Whistic-friendly / single artifact): a single, password-protected ZIP containing all PDFs + manifest.csv + checksums.txt. Provide the password to ACME out-of-band (we can send via secure OTP). Pros: one upload, clean package. Cons: some procurement tools flag passworded archives — confirm with your portal.

Packaging notes and our deliverables if you choose option 1 or 2:
- PDFs will be flattened and visually watermarked with: "For ACME Procurement - Confidential" in the page footer (semi-opaque, not metadata-only).
- We will produce both MD5 and SHA256 values in manifest_v3.csv plus a checksums_v3.txt (machine-friendly).
- We will include an audit_trace.txt with a simple packing log (file names, timestamps, packer version) to help procurement automation.
- We avoid embedding sensitive comments or hidden form fields that portal extractors sometimes choke on.

I’ve attached a draft bundle (redwood_sig_bundle_v3.pdf) and a sample manifest (manifest_v3.csv). Marissa, can you flatten + stamp the PDFs and produce the checksums? Neha, quick confirmation: any objection to visible watermarking language above, or encryption approach?

If ZIP is preferred we’ll password it and send an OTP; otherwise we’ll push individual files to the OneTrust upload link you provide.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Internal: ACME SIG packaging — checksums & watermarking (action items)

Team — looping you in for packaging work. Jared prefers whichever is fastest for ACME procurement; they mentioned OneTrust and Whistic. Actions below: 

1) Marissa: produce flattened, watermarked PDFs using the watermark string exactly: "For ACME Procurement - Confidential". Watermark should be a 10pt semi-opaque footer on each page (not an invisible overlay). File name should match pattern: redwood_SIG_<section>_v3.pdf.

2) Marissa: export both a single ZIP (redwood_SIG_ACME_20261112.zip) and the individual PDFs folder. Include manifest_v3.csv with columns: filename, md5, sha256, size_bytes, pages. Also include checksums_v3.txt (newline-delimited md5sum format).

3) Neha: confirm that visible watermarking is acceptable from a security/compliance standpoint (no PII insertion). Also advise on whether we should password-protect the ZIP by default; procurement may prefer a password for transport but some portals reject encrypted archives. NOTE: if we password the ZIP, include an audit_trace.txt and DO NOT embed the password in the manifest. We will send OTP separately.

4) Sergio: quick redaction pass on the SIG PDF (ensure no sample customer emails or screenshots with e-mail addresses). If anything looks sticky, flag it for removal.

Constraints: OneTrust sometimes removes PDF layers during ingestion — flattening is mandatory. Whistic tends to accept ZIPs but rejects passworded zips in some buyer accounts; we should be ready with both artifacts.

Attachments I’m including for reference: redwood_sig_bundle_v3.pdf (draft), manifest_v3.csv. 

Thanks — please push final artifacts to the shared S3 folder /acme/sig-packages/2026-11-12 when ready and ping me here.

Rishi
